title: The Mixed-Up Badge Party
markdown:
Mina the mouse wiggled her whiskers. “Lunchtime!” she squeaked. Beside her, Rowan the rook fluffed his feathers. “Caw! Cheese day, I hope!” he rumbled. Mina giggled. “Or maybe seed pudding?”

Today lunch was a little different. Mr Fitzwilliam, the new lunch helper, stood by the door with a basket of shiny badges. “Welcome!” he chirped. “Today, special colours! Red for Room One, Blue for Room Two, Green for Room Three, and Yellow for Room Four!”

Mina, from Room Two, took a blue badge. Rowan, from Room Four, chose yellow. But soon more students arrived, and the badges seemed to have a mind of their own. A boy from Room One liked the cheerful yellow badge, so he put it on. A girl from Room Three loved the sky-blue badge and swapped her green one. The neat line became a joyful rainbow. A badger from Room One chatted happily with a fox from Room Three, both wearing the wrong badges.

“Caw! This is exciting!” Rowan exclaimed. “Look, Mina, all the red ones are together!”

Mina blinked. “But Rowan, that’s a badger talking to a fox! And they’re wearing red badges…” A group with blue badges sang a happy song, forgetting all about the queue. It was a swirling parade of colours.

Mina’s Gran Elin watched with a gentle smile. “They all seem so happy, dear,” she said.

“But Gran,” Mina whispered, “the badges are mixed up.”

Gran Elin squeezed Mina’s paw. “Sometimes, Mina, the best order is what makes everyone happy. Perhaps these colours aren’t for telling people where to go, but for making a bright picture.”

Mina looked around. Rowan was chatting with a robin about worms. The singing group laughed and smiled. It was wonderful.

“Mr Fitzwilliam!” Mina squeaked. He hurried over. “The colours,” Mina pointed, “they’re making everyone smile! It’s like a party!”

Mr Fitzwilliam saw the laughing students and his neat basket of badges. A smile spread across his face. “A party, you say?” He let the basket go, and badges tumbled to the floor. “Well, then! Perhaps we should have a party!”

With a happy cheer, the students went into the canteen, wearing their mixed-up badges. They sat with new friends and ate lunch, surrounded by happy chatter. Cheerful colour, it turned out, led the way best. And Rowan ate extra cheese because it was cheese day, and the happy colourful mess made it taste even more delicious.
characters: Mina (a mouse), Rowan (a rook), Elin (a grandmother)
author: StoryGen Community
